title: SessionOpen
description: Open (or resume) a long-lived employee session on the node. ssh_servers: remote servers granted to the employee's role in this project (remote-servers.md §7), sent only when both sides have the ssh_gateway feature; omitted or empty means no SSH access.

prepare.description: Key of the git.prepare job that must have succeeded first.

prepare_jobs.description: Every git.prepare job (one per repository) that must have succeeded first; prepare is the first of them.

import.description: A session moved from another node (protocol.md §4.11): after prepare_jobs the daemon downloads GET /nodes/moves/{export_id}, checks size and sha256, writes the transcript under its own paths and restores the worktree snapshots, then resumes. Any failure answers session.opened {resume_failed}. Only sent to daemons with the session_move feature.

env.description: Extra non-secret environment; the daemon adds PATH/HOME/MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT/git credential variables itself.

context.description: Context management of the role (shared-members.md §5.1): the runtime compacts by itself at limit_tokens × in_task_pct / 100 (Codex: limit_tokens capped at window_tokens). Without limit_tokens the target is in_task_pct of window_tokens; without either, Codex keeps its own default and Claude applies in_task_pct to its effective window (window − 20K). Claude never compacts later than its effective window − 13K. focus is added to the instructions of such a compaction.

limit_tokens.description: The role's context limit in tokens.

window_tokens.description: The context window the runtime reported for this employee's last session (tokens), when known. Codex caps limit_tokens at it (a limit above the model's window would never trigger); without limit_tokens both runtimes take in_task_pct of it as the token target.

git_credentials.description: Install the credential helper and gh wrapper.

git_hosts.description: Standalone Git repositories' hosts this session may get credentials for (git-repos.md §5): HTTPS hosts get the credential helper, SSH hosts the git-ssh wrapper. Only with git_credentials.

host.description: host[:port], the port only when not the default.

fs.description: The shared folder (juicefs-shared-storage design), sent only when the node has the owner's volume mounted or an external mount (fs_mount / fs_external) and the owner has a ready volume: paths relative to the volume root. The daemon creates both directories when missing, adds them to the session's writable directories and exports AGENT_TEAMS_PROJECT_DIR / AGENT_TEAMS_SHARED_DIR. Omitted = no shared folder.

anchor.description: The anchor of the task the employee holds when the session (re)opens without a first_message anchor (a crash reopen, a reopen after a daemon restart): the new process starts with it, as if session.send had carried it.

skills.description: Skills of the employee's role. Claude: the daemon writes them as a local plugin outside the worktree and loads it (options.plugins + options.skills). Codex gets them in developer_instructions instead.

plugins.description: Plugins ticked on the employee's role, each at an exact version (architecture.md §6.5). The daemon writes each into a per-employee directory outside the worktree. Claude: loaded with options.plugins (skipMcpDiscovery), skills lists the plugin's skills and commands, and mcp_servers join options.mcpServers as plugin_<plugin>_<server>. Codex: only mcp_servers are used (the skill text is already in developer_instructions).

thread_no.description: The thread the session works in; null for the coordinator and a project member outside any thread.

scope.description: Where the employee belongs: "project" for the coordinator and the project members shared by every thread (skills and plugins live in <project>/project/<name>), "thread" for a lead or a member created with a thread. Absent from older consoles: a null thread_no means project.

tools.description: SDK options.tools; [] means no built-in tools.

allow_dangerously_skip_permissions.description: Required for bypassPermissions and session.set_mode to bypassPermissions.

read_only.description: Lead and read_only roles: enables bash_policy and a sandbox without writable paths.

deny_non_platform_tools.description: Coordinator: PreToolUse hook rejects everything except mcp__platform__* (and, with memory_files, the file tools inside the memory directories).

memory_files.description: The file tools (Read, Glob, Grep, Edit, Write) may also work inside the shared folder's memory directories (<project dir>/.memory and <shared dir>/.memory) even in a read-only or platform-only session; set only with fs.

prefer_auto.description: A session's employee: open in permission_mode, then switch to auto once the session's model reports supportsAutoMode (init.permission_mode says which it runs in).

BashPolicy.title: BashPolicy
BashPolicy.description: argv-parsed allow list for read-only sessions (not regex).

config.description: Extra thread/start config (e.g. sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots); mcp_servers.platform is filled in by the daemon.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for thread/start; null or absent: the model's default.

approvals_reviewer.description: Who reviews approval requests: auto_review lets Codex's reviewer subagent decide (a session's 自动 mode); absent: the user.

AntigravitySessionOptions.title: AntigravitySessionOptions
AntigravitySessionOptions.description: agy acp --process-per-session, one process per session. The ACP sessionId is kept as sdk_session_id (session.opened, ResumeRef, sessions.report).

model.description: Model slug (e.g. gemini-4-neon-high); empty leaves the choice to agy.

read_only.description: Read-only roles (reviewer…): the daemon disables agy's writing tools (deny rules for file writes and edits) and rejects every writing permission request; commands run only when bash_policy allows them.

approval.description: How ACP session/request_permission is answered when read_only does not already reject it. ask: forwarded to the console as approval.request; auto: the daemon allows it (bypass roles).

system_append.description: Appended to agy's system prompt (session/new _meta.antigravity.systemPrompt.append): platform rules, role instructions and skills inlined.

bash_policy.description: read_only: argv allow list for shell commands, as in claude.bash_policy.

images.description: Images to deliver with the text (at most 8), as session.send images (daemons without attachments_v2).

attachments.description: Attachments to deliver with the text, as session.send attachments (daemons with attachments_v2).

anchor.description: The task anchor, as session.send anchor.

files.description: Text files of the skill; SKILL.md is required.

path.description: Relative path inside the skill directory.

version.description: Library version number (1, 2, …); the directory is <name>@<version>.

files.description: Every file of the package, .claude-plugin/plugin.json included.

skills.description: Qualified names (<plugin>:<skill or command>) to add to options.skills.

mcp_servers.description: The plugin's MCP servers by name; ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is replaced by the plugin directory.

path.description: Relative path inside the plugin directory; '.' and '..' segments are refused.

encoding.description: utf8 (default) or base64 for binary files.
